Synopsis:
Swiss researchers and the Summit Foundation are testing wool blankets as a biodegradable alternative to plastic tarpaulins for slowing glacier melt on the Tsanfleuron Glacier. Early results show wool performs comparably to synthetic covers. The project addresses both environmental pollution from microplastics and the waste of Swiss wool. Scientists emphasize this is not a climate solution — only emissions reductions can meaningfully arrest long-term ice loss.
